name: MT-Video-Bench
abstract: MT-Video-Bench evaluates perception and interaction in multi-turn video dialogues. This page uses Overall from the main table and keeps the six sub-dimensions as auxiliary metrics.
contributions: The paper shows that even strong models remain far from saturated in multi-turn video dialogue.
The six sub-metrics help distinguish whether a model struggles more with perception or conversational interaction.
method: MT-Video-Bench moves video evaluation from single-turn QA to multi-turn dialogue, focusing on sustained understanding and interaction over videos.

It defines six core competencies around perceptivity and interactivity, and curates 1,000 multi-turn video dialogues from diverse domains aligned with realistic applications such as sports analysis and intelligent tutoring.
The paper shows large performance gaps between open-source and closed-source MLLMs, while also exposing weaknesses in long-horizon tracking and interactive consistency.
MT-Video-Bench therefore serves as an important bridge between standard video QA and more realistic video-agent settings.
leaderboard_note: The primary leaderboard uses Overall from the main table. The OR/MR/CS/AR/TS/PI subdimensions are kept to support the paper-oriented supplementary sections below.
